subject: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@finly.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we agreed on. Please let me know if I missed anything or if you want a slightly different framing.

Key pain points you shared:
- Streaming UX feels sluggish: end-users see long pauses between streaming chunks; developers report ~700ms p95 chunk latency today.
- Overall p95 latency for short prompts (~<512 tokens) spikes during peak times.
- Concurrency bottlenecks: your current infra starts queueing and failing around ~250 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Cost predictability and the ability to run in a VPC are must-haves for procurement.

Current stack (as described):
- In-house transformer service on G4-like instances; custom batching layer but limited KV cache support.
- Frontend uses client-side streaming but relies on server to push tokens; any backpressure increases perceived latency.
- No dedicated autoscaling for streaming endpoints.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- p95 <= 200ms for short prompts (<512 tokens) across normal traffic patterns.
- Streaming chunk latency consistently <100ms between emitted chunks for a good UX (end-to-end token delivery).
- Sustain 500 concurrent streaming users (spike to 750) without p95 exceeding 250ms.
- Ability to run in your VPC and meet SOC2 requirements for procurement.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- I will share a proposed bench + PoC plan that outlines test harness, target traffic profiles, and required Redwood config (attached). (Marissa / today EOD)
- Aditya to draft a technical deep-dive agenda focused on streaming kernel selection, KV caching, and autoscaling options. (Aditya / Wed)
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team next Friday — please confirm availability. (Samir / Finly)
- Procurement checklist: I’ll include SOC2 and standard security artifacts in the next email. (Marissa / Tue)

Attachments: redwood-p95-bench-plan.pdf (bench plan + configuration suggestions)

If this looks good I’ll queue the PoC plan and Aditya will follow up about infra specifics.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform

From: Samir Patel <samir@finly.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena@finly.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 13:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the plan. High level — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 700ms p95 is measured from our edge to first token (we’ll share the raw telemetry file). We see the biggest degradation on high concurrency spikes (end of day batch jobs + interactive users).
- Our internal SLA target for interactive UIs is to stay under 200ms p95; the streaming chunk threshold you call out (<100ms) is where we see a meaningful UX improvement.
- Procurement: procurement timeline is 6–8 weeks; SOC2 report and a basic security questionnaire will be required for internal review.

Next steps for us:
- I attached the telemetry export (finly-telemetry.csv) and a short doc with our traffic patterns.
- Please include a cost-ballpark for a 6-month PoC (expected 250–500 concurrent) so we can surface the ask to procurement.
- We’re available for a deep-dive next Friday afternoon (US Eastern).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Infra | Finly
samir@finly.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Marissa / Dylan —

Noting Samir confirmed telemetry and procurement window. My take / immediate actions: 

- I’ll own the PoC bench: reproduce Finly’s workload (streaming + interactive bursts) with our harness and measure p95 token latency and concurrency scaling. Deliverable: bench results + recommended config (quantization profile, batching policy, cache settings). ETA: EOD Thu.
- Dylan, can you draft a minimal Dedicated capacity estimate for 6 months (250–500 sustained concurrent, burst to 750) and include regional node selection (us-east preference)? Use DL-7421 as the deal id.
- Marissa, I’ll include a short SOC2 artifact summary and standard security one-pager for procurement.

I’ll copy the bench artifacts into the shared PoC link: https://redwood.app/s/finly/poCs/7421.

Aditya
